value_derivation.role: Penalize z-axis base linear velocity using an L2 squared kernel (Isaac Lab v2.3.1, reports/evidence/go2_reward_term_roles_20260917/isaaclab_envs_mdp_rewards.py: torch.square(asset.data.root_lin_vel_b[:, 2])). It is the body frame's vertical speed squared - not foot height, not world-frame altitude, not ground clearance. On a slope the body frame tilts with the robot, so the same climb charges differently there than on flat ground.
value_derivation.walk_margin: G-A033 walk margin +0.1359 -> +0.1540 at -1.25 (reports/evidence/go2_reward_mechanism_20260917/PROBES.csv, zone WALK, delta +0.0181, range_status OUT_OF_RANGE - beyond the walking values -2.0, -1.75 and -1.5). The stop zone's top is +0.0155, so the margin stays about ten times above it. A margin is reward arithmetic over measured postures; since the 2026-09-26 revision of reports/GO2_REWARD_MECHANISM_FORECAST.md section 8 it is not a ranking basis.
value_derivation.situations: reports/evidence/go2_reward_mechanism_20260917/PROBE_SITUATIONS.csv at -1.25: walk +0.0181, climb +0.0386, sway -0.0705, push -0.0578. The sheet's post-hoc direction hits are 10 of 19 cumulative (A038 3/3, A043 4/8, A047 3/8; non-independent cells, not a statistical test); G-A043 went the opposite way on sway and on three of four push directions. The cells are carried as a record, not as a prediction this arm relies on.
value_derivation.rule: -1.25 keeps the 0.25 interval of the three measured points (-2.0, -1.75, -1.5) and steps once beyond the relaxed end. value_derivation.not_claimed: No score gain is estimated and no improvement is predicted. A failure at -1.25 does not make G-A043's -1.5 result luck, and a success does not identify its cause.

hypothesis.edge_rule: Avoiding falsification is not support: a value just inside a boundary (for example 11 of 96 at 15 cm or 58 rough falls) is INSUFFICIENT, as the thresholds already say.
decisions: stairs and rough SUPPORTED, yaw cost ABSENT, adoption met: first promotion candidate; an independent-seed replicate is the next question.
stairs and rough SUPPORTED, yaw cost PRESENT: gain and cost observed together at two values of this dial; the next design reduces that cost (not recommended now).

stairs and rough NOT_SUPPORTED: the gain did not appear at -1.25; this does not make -1.5 luck (a non-linear response explains it too). Stop extending this dial's range and leave the -1.5 replicate to U2.

any other mix (e.g. hypothesis supported but adoption failed on G4/G6/G7 or a flat guard, only one of stairs/rough supported, only the yaw cost insufficient): record per-indicator verdicts, re-compare the next candidates by the failed axis, do not collapse into one INCONCLUSIVE, do not rerun automatically.

why: Purpose: extend the observed range of the one dial in this campaign with direct evidence of moving both the stairs and the rough axis on this baseline, and record whether the G2 combined-turn cost moves with it. Not a promise of a higher score.

Role first (Isaac Lab formula): lin_vel_z_l2 pays -w * v_z^2 in the body frame, with no direction term, so the rise a tread requires is charged at the same rate as the bounce a bad landing produces. That is the mechanism this arm moves, and it is a property of the formula.

What is measured: at -2.0 / -1.75 / -1.5 the 15 cm ge1 count rose 4 -> 39 -> 88 of 96 and ge2 0 -> 0 -> 77, while rough side-step posture falls went 59 -> 80 -> 24 and combined_yaw_right falls 0 -> 0 -> 29. The stair counters are monotone in the weight; the fall counters are not.

G-A043's loss is a rare posture collapse during the right turn: 29 of 96 robots, all through the tilt and height channels together, 0 terminations, fall times 2.46-19.8 s. The fallers' mean profile shows lateral velocity and tilt growing about 1.5 s before the verdict and the yaw-rate sign flipping last. It was observed only on G-A043 and this data cannot separate its cause.

Why -1.25: it keeps the 0.25 interval of the measured points and steps once beyond the relaxed end. That is an operational choice, not an optimum estimate; -1.0 is G-A037's held value and further out.

Two verdicts, fixed before the run: the hypothesis indicators (stairs 15 cm ge2 >= 50 supported / <= 10 not; rough side-step falls <= 41 supported / >= 59 not; combined_yaw_right falls at >= 2 seeds = cost present, 0 seeds = absent) and adoption under fact_rules_v1 plus post_a043_push4_v1 with every G-A044 threshold. Neither verdict rescues the other.
Collection is G-A044's: all 69 cases in one pass, both combined-turn directions and all four push directions filmed on the candidate, every baseline counterpart reused by SHA.

lin_vel_z_l2.role: Penalize z-axis base linear velocity using L2 squared kernel. [isaaclab_envs_mdp_rewards.py:76]
lin_vel_z_l2.out_of_range_reason: -1.25 is one 0.25 interval beyond the relaxed end of the three walking values (-2.0, -1.75, -1.5). The run exists to extend the observed range; it is exploratory and its hypothesis thresholds are fixed before the run.

walk_margin.reason: Two situation cells are negative at -1.25 (sway, push) while climb and walk are positive - the same shape as -1.5 at a larger size. The sheet got sway and three push directions backwards at -1.5, so the cells are carried as a record. The losing axes are guarded anyway: rough as a scored group and a hypothesis indicator, all four push directions in the protection block, all filmed.

inference.rule: fact-based inference chain (2026-09-17 user instruction; MASTER section 5, AGENTS 4-9); a point-gain estimate is not required
inference.role: Isaac Lab v2.3.1 lin_vel_z_l2 (reports/evidence/go2_reward_term_roles_20260917/isaaclab_envs_mdp_rewards.py) pays -w * v_z^2 measured in the body frame. The square has no sign and the frame has no direction term, so rising onto a tread and bouncing after a bad landing are charged by the same expression; the weight is the only thing that separates how much either costs.

rows.reads: the relaxed end of the three measured walking values: 15 cm ge2 0 -> 77 of 96, 15 cm ge1 88, rough side-step posture falls 59 -> 24. This is the direct evidence that this dial moves both the stairs and the rough axis on this baseline - and in the same row the cost: combined_yaw_right falls 0 -> 29.

the midpoint: the 15 cm ge1 count already rose 4 -> 39 while ge2 stayed 0. Across the three points the stair counters are monotone in the weight (ge1 4 -> 39 -> 88), which is what makes one more interval on the same side an observation worth having.

the cost indicator's anchor: G-A043 lost 9, 9 and 11 robots on combined_yaw_right, every one through the tilt and height channels together. G-A033, G-A044 and G-A047 lost none on either turn direction.

reward arithmetic at -1.25: walk margin +0.1359 -> +0.1540, zone WALK, range_status OUT_OF_RANGE. It rules out a standing policy by arithmetic and supports nothing else; since the 2026-09-26 section 8 revision it is not a ranking basis.

the frozen baseline this arm starts from carries this dial at -2.0, walks (POLICY_LOCOMOTES) and scores 42.52861/70 over 69 cases with terrain level 4.7087 at iteration 999. G-A043's harvest adds the second walking value of this dial and is not yet in this ledger file.

contradicting.reads: the midpoint was worse than both ends on the fall counters: rough side-step 59 -> 80, 10 cm stairs falls 34 -> 65, four-direction push falls 22 -> 66, total 42.52861 -> 38.89379. The fall response to this dial is non-monotone, so nothing predicts the falls at -1.25.

the whole loss of G-A043 sits in one axis and one case: G2's scenario proxy fell 0.87742 -> 0.43581 (weighted -4.63693/70) and the binding case is combined_yaw_right at seed 303 on BOTH arms, so the axis did not change which case holds it down - that case simply got worse.

contradicting.key: S5 오르기 수직 벌점 몫 대 15cm 오르기
contradicting.reads: the between-run test of the rule the original relaxation argument rested on. It still reports False, and it is the row that put G-A037 (-1.0) on hold. G-A043's stair result does not rescue that rule - it shows this weight moves the stairs on THIS baseline, not that the penalty share orders climbing across runs.

the situation arithmetic this spec carries at -1.25 (sway -0.0705) got the direction wrong at -1.5: it predicted sway down and the rough side-step proxy rose +0.295513. The -1.25 cells are a record, not evidence.

inference.singularity: One dial, three measured walking values on one baseline, and two different shapes: the stair counters rise monotonically as the penalty relaxes (15 cm ge1 4 -> 39 -> 88) while every fall counter is non-monotone (rough side-step 59 -> 80 -> 24, push 22 -> 66 -> 10) and the combined right-turn cost appears only at the relaxed end (0 -> 0 -> 29). Whether the gain and the cost continue together beyond -1.5 is unmeasured.

walk.basis: PROBES.csv at -1.25: walk margin +0.1359 -> +0.1540, zone WALK, about ten times the stop zone's top +0.0155. All three measured values walked. This rules out a standing policy and supports nothing else.

climb.basis: observed on this baseline, not computed: the 15 cm ge1 count rose 4 -> 39 -> 88 of 96 across -2.0 / -1.75 / -1.5 (DIAL_THREE_POINTS.csv). The direction beyond -1.5 is an extrapolation of a monotone counter; its size, and whether it saturates or reverses, is unknown.

sway.basis: the rough side-step fall counter was non-monotone across the three walking values (59 -> 80 -> 24), and the arithmetic cell (-0.0705) got the direction wrong at -1.5. No direction is claimed; the hypothesis indicator reads it.

push.basis: four-direction push falls were non-monotone (22 -> 66 -> 10) and the arithmetic predicted a loss at -1.5 that did not appear in three of four directions. No direction is claimed; all four directions stay in the protection block.

inference.falsified_if: Hypothesis (tools/go2_dial_hypothesis.py, thresholds fixed in preregistered.hypothesis): the stairs half is refuted if the pooled 15 cm ge2 count is 10 of 96 or fewer, the rough half if rough side-step posture falls are 59 or more; values between the lines are INSUFFICIENT, not near-support. The yaw cost is recorded, not refuted: present at two or more seeds with a posture fall, absent at none. Adoption is separate: every G-A044 criterion under fact_rules_v1 plus post_a043_push4_v1. A refuted hypothesis at -1.25 does not make G-A043's -1.5 result luck; it closes further range extension of this dial.
inference.seed_limit: Every training run used seed 42 and no seed replicate exists, so a result supports or refutes the exploratory hypothesis at this value on this path; it does not fix a lever effect (reports/GO2_SEED_SENSITIVITY.md section 5). The replicate is the v10 pair, open decision U2-SEED-REPLICATE-20260918.
inference.status_reason: INFORMATION_RUN: -1.25 is outside the observed walking range, the fall response of this dial is non-monotone across the three measured points, the cause of G-A043's combined-turn loss is unidentified, and the forecast sheet got two of four situations backwards at -1.5. The run extends the observation range; it does not recommend a value.
inference.counterevidence_response: The adverse rows are carried, not footnoted: G-A044's non-monotone falls, G-A043's G2 loss, the S5 row against the original relaxation argument and the forecast sheet's wrong direction. The design responds by fixing hypothesis thresholds as counts before the run and keeping them separate from adoption, by keeping every adoption threshold where G-A044 had it (the per-case flat survival limit of 0.0625 is the rule that caught G-A043's loss), by collecting all 69 cases in one pass, and by filming both combined-turn directions so a survival number cannot stand in for the behaviour.
